compounding_issues: Hardcoded `SECRET_KEY` default (dev-secret-key) introduced in Session 2 was never hardened across later sessions
Email integration in Session 3 uses fake address (`{username}@example.com`) and top-level Celery import couples the web app to broker availability
Rate-limit key function in Session 5 duplicates JWT token-parsing logic already present in `token_required` instead of reusing it
Repository `update()` builds dynamic SQL column names from dict keys, safe only because call sites hardcode the keys
Session 2 schema migration (CREATE TABLE + ALTER TABLE fallback via PRAGMA) is workable but fragile for future schema drift
key_decisions: Session 2 baked a user ownership model into the schema (owner_id FK, JWT+bcrypt auth) which every later session depended on
Session 3 introduced Celery async email notifications on task completion, adding Redis as an external integration point
Session 4 extracted a repository pattern (UserRepository/TaskRepository with ABC base), slimming app.py and separating data access from routes
Session 5 layered Flask-Limiter rate limiting (user-keyed via JWT) and cursor-based pagination on top of the repo layer
Maintained a single Flask app.py as the growth container for 3 sessions before paying down structure debt in the refactor
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the 5 sessions in a classic S-curve. Session 1 delivered a clean CRUD baseline with 18 tests; Session 2 stacked authentication and ownership on top; Session 3 added async integration; Session 4 was a pure internal-quality refactor that preserved the 44-test surface while extracting a repository layer and shrinking app.py; Session 5 added production cross-cutting concerns (rate limiting, pagination) and grew tests to 56, all passing. The refactor in Session 4 traded feature velocity for architecture and directly enabled the clean pagination implementation in Session 5, so the arc is a healthy foundation-to-hardening progression with no observable degradation.
story_review.summary: A well-sequenced greenfield-to-hardening story where each session's choices built coherently on the prior state, with the Session 4 repository refactor cleanly enabling Session 5's cross-cutting work.
